title: Financial Services Vertical Playbook — Enterprise
author: Ava Martinez
content:
Overview:

This playbook equips field sellers and solutions engineers to position Redwood Inference for large financial-services (FinServ) customers. It synthesizes messaging, competitive counterpoints, a tiered pricing guide, a repeatable deal motion, a short case study to cite, and a security FAQ tailored to regulated buyers (banks, payments providers, insurance carriers).

Use cases targeted in this playbook:
- Real-time customer support assistants with SSO and PII redaction
- Document ingestion and summarization for credit underwriting and compliance
- Transactional assistant (KYC flows, approval automation) with rigorous audit trails
- Risk-scoring and structured extraction pipelines with drift detection

Target personas and buying committee:
- Head of Data Science / ML: cares about model fidelity, evals, and rollback controls
- Platform/Infrastructure Lead: cares about latency, throughput, autoscaling, and private deployment options
- Head of Security/Compliance: cares about data residency, audit logging, KMS, and FedRAMP/ISO posture
- Product Manager (Payments/Loans): cares about feature velocity, UX, and cost predictability
- Procurement/Legal: contract terms, SLAs, indemnities

Core value props (elevator variants):
1) For engineering teams: "Ship predictable LLM features at production scale — low latency, explicit cost controls, and the same API across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments."
2) For security/compliance: "Isolate sensitive workloads with Redwood Private: customer-managed VPCs, KMS integrations, and audit-grade logging for regulated operations."
3) For finance leaders: "Cut per-token inference spend with workload-aware batching, caching, and quantization recommendations that preserve quality while reducing unit costs."

Positioning pillars (3):
- Production economics: show measurable per-request cost reductions and predictable capacity options (Dedicated contracts)
- Unified runtime: single API and rollout semantics across deployment modes — reduces integration and ops friction
- Reliability & graceful degradation: automatic model fallbacks, regional routing, and SLO-backed commitments for enterprise customers

Competitive brief (high-level):
| Competitor | Typical Strength | Redwood Counterpoint |
|---|---|---|
| Large public cloud managed endpoints | Deep cloud integration, broad marketplace | Redwood provides superior inference-specific optimizations (KV caching, batching, custom kernels) and deployment flexibility (private/on-prem variants) with transparent latency & cost profiles |
| LLM API pure-play | Simplicity, model breadth | Redwood matches API simplicity but adds production controls: Dedicated capacity, rollouts, and cost optimization tooling |
| Self-hosted inference vendors | Full control on-prem | Redwood’s Private option offers a packaged control plane + auditability without the engineering lift of building an orchestration/runtime stack in-house |

Differentiator proof points to cite in sales meetings:
- Benchmarked 2–4x latency improvement on common customer prompts vs naive GPU endpoints via continuous batching and optimized kernels
- Documented per-token cost savings from prefix caching and quantization recommendations (typical 30–60% reduction on retrieval-augmented workloads)
- Enterprise customers using Dedicated report predictable 99.95% regional availability in Q4 deployments (internal SLA telemetry)

Pricing guidance (tiered and negotiation play):
- Hosted (pay-as-you-go): per-token generation + per-1000 embedding unit. Use for PoCs and low-volume production.
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): monthly committed GPU units with predictable throughput. Offer 12/24-month commitments with step-down pricing and burst allowances.
- Private (enterprise license): platform fee + per-node runtime license; support tiers add audit log retention and SOC2/FedRAMP packaging.

Suggested pricing table (sales guidance ranges; always check legal/pricing sheet for final numbers):
| Offering | Typical buyer | Guidance model | Walkaway negotiation levers |
|---|---|---|---|
| Hosted | Startups, small product teams | List per-token, incremental volume discounts | Add monthly committed spend to convert to Dedicated credit |
| Dedicated | Mid-market to Enterprise | Commit X GPUs/month -> Y cents per 1k tokens (lower than hosted) | Contract term length, burst pool sizing, training/onboarding credits |
| Private | Regulated enterprise | Annual platform fee + per-node license | Multi-year contract, audit package pricing, managed services hours |

Deal motion: step-by-step (repeatable):
1) Qualification checklist (SE): compliance constraints, latency SLO needs, monthly token volume estimate, sample prompt/seq length distribution, required regions
2) Tech validation (POC): 2–4 week POC using Hosted or Dedicated trial; enrich with 3 canonical prompts, latency/cost targets, and success criteria (accuracy/SLO)
3) Security review: provide Private architecture diagram, KMS integration notes, sample audit logs format, and a routing/segmentation plan
4) Procurement & contracting: suggest standard Redwood enterprise SLA and IP terms; use addendums for strict data residency or on-prem installation terms
5) Onboarding & rollout: recommend canary rollout plan (10% traffic -> 50% -> 100%) with automatic fallback policy and post-rollout quality checks

Checklist: required artifacts for enterprise deals:
- Sample prompts and token distribution CSV
- Representative latency and throughput SLOs
- Compliance questionnaire answers (SOC2/GDPR clauses)
- Network architecture (VPC peering/firewall rules)
- KMS and key rotation policy notes

Short case study (anonymized):
- Customer: Large North American bank (anonymized)
- Problem: Slow, manual document intake for commercial loan origination — 72-hour turnaround, human error in data extraction
- Approach: Deployed Redwood Private in customer VPC; used RAG and structured extraction pipeline; KV caching of common legal clauses
- Outcome: Reduced intake time to 4 hours for 85% of cases; 38% fewer downstream exceptions; measurable reduction in per-application inference cost after enabling batching and quantization profiles

Security FAQ (targeted answers for prospect RFIs and security reviews):
Q: Can we keep all data within our cloud account?
A: Yes — Redwood Private supports customer-managed VPC deployments and on-prem packages. The control plane can be configured as a private, customer-hosted endpoint for full data residency.

Q: How are keys and secrets managed?
A: We integrate with AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, and customer HSMs. Keys for Private deployments remain in the customer's KMS. For Dedicated/Hosted, we provide configurable envelope encryption and detailed key rotation logs.

Q: What audit logging is available?
A: Token-level logs, request/response metadata, model-version used, routing decisions, and admin actions are available. Logs can be streamed to customer SIEMs (S3/Blob/third-party collectors) with configurable retention.

Q: How do you prevent data leakage across tenants?
A: Multi-tenant isolation by default for Hosted — redaction pipelines, strict token policies, and per-tenant KV namespaces. Dedicated and Private deployments provide physical or network isolation.

Q: Do you support explainability or provenance for model outputs?
A: We capture model version, prompt set, and evaluation snapshot for each rollout. We also support structured outputs and can attach provenance metadata to generated tokens for traceability.

Q: What compliance certifications are supported?
A: Redwood maintains SOC2 Type II evidence and provides artifacts to customers; Private deployment packaging supports customer-specific compliance drives (FedRAMP/PCI/SOX readiness) with professional services for gap remediation.

Objection handling (brief cues):
- "We already have a self-hosted stack": emphasize total cost of ownership, time-to-market, and engineering burden of maintaining optimized inference (kernels, batching, KV cache). Offer pilot and migration plan.
- "Model quality concerns": propose an eval plan with baseline prompt sets, A/B rollouts, and regression alerts in Redwood Optimize.
- "Pricing seems opaque": provide worked examples using the customer’s token estimates and show Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private cost curves.

Appendix: recommended POC success criteria (example):
1) Latency: p95 < 300ms for defined prompt set
2) Cost: per-inference cost reduction >= 20% vs customer baseline after applying caching/quantization
3) Accuracy: core extraction F1 >= 0.92 on holdout set
4) Compliance: sample audit logs delivered to customer SIEM and verified
